messages:
morgan.s: FYI — after the 07:00 driver rollout to 535.86 in us-west-2 we've got ~40% of H100 pods failing at model start; symptoms: ptxas/ptx verification errors and intermittent NCCL hangs. Opening a thread for triage.

infra-bot: deploy-bot pushed node-driver-upgrade/535.86 to us-west-2 at 2027-05-03T07:02:00Z. Canary passed (small batch) and then rollout auto-continued.

alessandra: Seeing lots of pods stuck in ContainerCreating with logs -> "ptx module verification failed: ptx version mismatch". Also multiple allreduce hangs (jobs stuck at ncclCommInitRank) for distributed training tasks.

raj.patel: Pasted kernel/log snippets:
```
$ dmesg | tail -n 40
[ 12345.678901] nvidia: ptxas fatal: Unknown PTX version '7.8'
[ 12345.679003] nvidia: failed to load ptx module for sm_90: compile failure
[ 12345.679105] nvidia: enqueue u64 remap error
```
And kubectl logs from a failing pod: "NCCL WARN : Init failure, timeout waiting for all ranks"

Also `nvidia-smi` on node: driver 535.86, CUDA 12.2 installed on host. But most containers still bundle CUDA 12.1 runtime.

jia_wu: This looks like a PTX/CUDA runtime mismatch: the driver now accepts PTX version X that our container toolchain can't produce or ptxas in the container is older. SM90 kernels get PTX code paths that require newer assembler. When ptxas fails the device falls back and NCCL sometimes deadlocks during ucx/ib init.

morgan.s: Quick Qs — which node pools are impacted, and can we isolate by image tag? Also what's the blast radius (inference vs training vs batch)?

alessandra: Impact: primarily h100-pool-3 and h100-staging; training jobs in us-west-2 hitting allreduce; inference fleet falling back to slower CPU-only in some pods (high latency). Non-H100 pools (A100) are unaffected.

raj.patel: Workarounds I'm trying now: 1) cordon/evict affected nodes, 2) force-schedule to older H100 pool with pre-535 driver, 3) set NODE_LABEL to avoid H100 for critical inference. Command:
```
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-7-45 && kubectl drain ip-10-0-7-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
kubectl annotate node ip-10-0-7-45 infra.redwood/driver-rollback=true
```

ops-oncall: We should also disable autoscaler from adding more upgraded nodes until we confirm fix — putting a hold on nodepool autoscale for us-west-2.

jia_wu: Longer term fixes: either rebuild our CUDA images with an updated ptxas (match driver/CUDA toolchain), or roll the driver back to the previous 535.45 that was compatible. Immediate route is rollback driver on affected nodepool (we have a daemonset that can do that fast) or patch DaemonSet to use host-cubin (precompiled sm90) when possible.

morgan.s: Cost/ops note — rollback will increase short-term toil and may require reboots; keeping capacity offline hurts reserved utilization. If we block H100, we need to shift inference to Dedicated reservations in eu-west-1/us-east-1 temporarily (traffic routing change). Anyone have an estimate of lost qps if we remove us-west-2 H100?

alessandra: Quick estimate: removing H100 in us-west-2 drops overall embedding throughput by ~25% during peak. Will trigger cost because more requests will go to more expensive dedicated fallback or smaller GPUs.

raj.patel: Opened a ticket with NVIDIA (SR# 999778) and attached ptxas logs + nvidia-bug-report. They acknowledged possible PTX/ptxas mismatch after driver 535.xx for SM90 and recommended either updating container ptxas or using the driver rollback.

jia_wu: Testing a hotfix: rebuild one inference image with CUDA toolkit 12.2 ptxas and push to canary tag. Early signs: container now compiles PTX successfully and model starts. If this passes for a few hours we can rollout image update instead of driver rollback.

morgan.s: Good. For triage plan: (1) Pause autoscaler + stop driver rollout (already flagged), (2) cordon affected nodes, (3) canary image rebuild with updated ptxas -> monitor, (4) if canary fails, schedule driver rollback for h100-pool-3.

infra-bot: Incident created: #INC-2027-045 — H100 PTX/NCCL regressions in us-west-2. Priority: P1. Pager duty alerted.

ops-oncall: I'm taking pager. Will coordinate rollback window if canary image doesn't stabilize by 09:30 PT.

alessandra: Noted a subtle networking symptom: when ptxas fails we sometimes also see repeated mlx5 error logs (ibv_post_send failures). Could be interplay causing NCCL to trap. Logged that to the ticket.

raj.patel: Follow-ups: collecting full set of failing pod IDs and node names, uploading to shared folder: s3://redwood-debug/2027-05-03/h100-ptx-regress/. Will add kube-describe + dmesg + nvidia-bug-report bundles.

morgan.s: Thanks all. Keep updates in this thread. If you find a clean mitigation (image vs driver rollback) post results. :thumbsup:
